summary: The frozen history test rejected every pre-registered stock rule: each beat only a small share of random baskets from the same list, and holding every name equally beat every rule and the core. Setup checks and past strength have shown no edge here. The four calls stay neutral with low conviction; Amgen and Gilead are now stretched after a fast run, which the house rules say never to chase. Nothing here is expected to beat the index; real money stays in the whole-market plan.
eli5: Two of the brain's runners, Amgen and Gilead, sprinted very fast this week and are out of breath. The house rule says never to chase a runner like that. Picking runners did no better than luck before, so the brain only watches with pretend money, and the family's real money keeps going into the whole-market basket.
letter:
Dear family,

First, real money. Nothing to do today; the weekly buy of the whole-market fund comes on the first trading day of next week, as always. Money we may need soon stays safe. The market's trend leans down a little; that is ordinary weather.

Second, the pretend game. Every stock rule we wrote down in advance lost to baskets picked at random from the same list, so our stock calls stay neutral. The weekly bet game stands at one week won and one lost, and this week's bet is ahead so far. A coin would do as well over so few weeks.

Third, a lesson. Two of our names ran up so fast this week that they now count as stretched. When something has just leapt, the urge to jump on is strongest, and that is exactly when our house rule says to wait. Buying after a sprint means paying for the good news twice.

Fourth, what would change our minds: a rule that beats random picks on history and then keeps a paper record ahead of the whole market for at least half a year. Until then we stay patient.

With care, the brain

bets.why: This week's bet was already placed and is repeated unchanged: names above their trend passing the setup checks, against names below their trend whose checklist leans down. No rule like this has beaten luck, so it is a learning bet only.

pick.thesis: Amgen sits at its high for the year and leads the benchmark on every window, and the chart checklist leans up with volume confirming. What changed is that a sharp run over the last month has left it stretched above its average and no longer calm, so it fails one setup check and the house rule says never to chase it. Names passing the setup checks did no better in the base rates, and every rule was rejected. Neutral and low, unchanged.

Its swings have widened, so a fast pullback is common after a run like this.
No earnings date in the pack, so a report could land inside the horizon unseen.
Moves partly with Gilead, which ran up at the same time, so the two are partly one bet.
